1.consolidated_definition: Gossipium hirsutum. Planta familia de las malváceas, o algodonero, que produce el algodón. Hay algunas variedades que se han cultivado en Puerto Rico. La del país corresponde al sarobei indígena. El algodón tuvo extenso cultivo en la época precolombina y durante la colonización. Se imponía como tributo a los indios, al igual que el oro. Se producía mayormente en la costa norte y también en las regiones de Coamo, Ponce y San Germán. Hubo épocas de exportación de este producto en el siglo XVII, decayendo en el XVIII. Recuperó en el siglo XIX, cuando se fomentó su cultivo. En épocas sucesivas se importaron nuevas variedades de Estados Unidos de América, y ya en el primer cuarto del siglo XX era extensamente cultivado en Isabela, Arecibo y otras zonas del país. Luego de una época de decadencia, debido a los daños del gusano rosado, ha dejado de cultivarse.
1.en_consolidated_definition: Gossipium hirsutum. Plant of the Malvaceae family, or cotton plant, which produces cotton. There are some varieties that have been cultivated in Puerto Rico. The one from the country corresponds to the sarobei indigenous variety. Cotton had extensive cultivation during pre-Columbian times and during colonization. It was imposed as a tribute on the Indians, just like gold. It was produced mainly in northern coast and also in Coamo, Ponce, and San Germán regions. There were periods of exportation of this product in the 17th century, declining in the 18th. It recovered in the 19th century, when its cultivation was promoted. In successive eras new varieties from the United States of America were imported, and by the first quarter of the 20th century it was extensively cultivated in Isabela, Arecibo, and other areas of the country. After a period of decline due to damage caused by the pink bollworm, it has ceased to be cultivated.
